issue.title: Long-lived ACE's pinned SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS overrides newer saved flag state in every descendant process
issue.description:
PROBLEM: `install_process_feature_flags()` exports the launching process's fully
resolved flag snapshot into `SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS` (`apply_feature_flags_env`,
src/sase/feature_flags/snapshot.py + env.py), and `resolve_feature_flags`
(src/sase/feature_flags/resolver.py) ranks env above saved state. A long-lived
interactive ACE therefore freezes flag resolution at its own start time and vetoes
every later `sase flag enable/disable` for **all** of its descendants: agent runners
(run_agent_runner's own `install_process_feature_flags()` re-resolves, but the
inherited env pin still wins), durable-op subprocesses, and gate-answer handoffs.
There is no refresh path short of restarting ACE.

OBSERVED 2026-09-15 (athena): ACE pid 3848459 started 2026-09-13 16:57 with
`agent_sudo_requests:false` pinned in its env. The flag was enabled in saved state
(`~/.sase/feature_flags.json`, mtime 2026-09-15 08:02). At 11:18 Bryan pressed
Authenticate on sudo gate sudo-5617dc91-e3a2-4561-ae42-d985f8e8135e (epic sase-110
phase sase-110.7's athena policy work): the spawned `sase sudo answer <id> --run
--json` inherited the stale pin, failed `require_sudo_requests_enabled` with
`feature_disabled`, and ACE showed the generic "Sudo handoff failed; gate remains
pending" toast — no sudo/PAM prompt, epic work blocked. The diagnosing agent's own
environment had inherited the same stale `false` pin through the ACE process tree,
confirming propagation beyond the handoff path.

A tale plan proposed the same day fixes only the sudo-handoff call site (drops
`SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS` from that one child env) plus error surfacing; this bead owns
the systemic decision. The pinning itself is deliberate (epic sase-nb decision 7:
launch-time consistency for an agent's whole run), so the fix needs a design choice,
e.g.: (a) interactive/long-lived surfaces (ACE) re-resolve and refresh their pin at
spawn boundaries instead of process start; (b) hosts spawning human-initiated
actions drop the inherited pin so children re-resolve from saved state; (c) the pin
carries its resolution timestamp and `sase doctor` / spawn sites warn or refuse on
staleness; (d) pin only for agent-run consistency, never for the interactive TUI
process itself. Whatever is chosen must preserve single-run flag consistency for
agents and keep both-flag-state testability.

task_type_fields.impact: Any flag change made while ACE runs is silently ignored by everything ACE spawns; on 2026-09-15 it blocked the sase-110.7 sudo authentication handoff (gate sudo-5617dc91) with a generic failure toast.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/feature_flags/snapshot.py install_process_feature_flags / apply_feature_flags_env; resolver env-over-saved precedence in src/sase/feature_flags/resolver.py
task_type_fields.repro: Start ACE, then flip a beta flag with sase flag enable <key>; run any 'sase <cmd>' child from ACE (e.g. the sudo answer handoff) and observe it still resolves the old value because the inherited SASE_FEATURE_FLAGS pin outranks ~/.sase/feature_flags.json. Concrete instance: ACE pid 3848459 (started 2026-09-13) vs agent_sudo_requests enabled 2026-09-15 08:02.
